### ¶ The Fourth Distinction on the Significations of Cancer ♋, in like manner to the former.

**L**et us say, therefore, that when its significations are those we have spoken of, it signifies that there will appear in the cities over which the <term>Almuztuali</term> <note>original: "alm uztauli"; referring to the planet that holds the most essential and accidental dignity or "dominion" over a specific place at a given time</note> rules a great many instances of mating and the bearing of children, as well as journeys, changes, and the transformation of things from one state of being to another. 

Consequently, there shall be famine and poverty on account of drought; and the people's fear of their enemies shall be increased. <term>Buboes</term> <note>original: "bubones"; inflammatory swellings of the lymph nodes, a primary symptom of the bubonic plague</note> and death shall fall upon them. It will be a lean year <note>original: "annus subtilis"; literally a "subtle" or "thin" year, implying scarcity or hardship</note> for men because of the many things that will happen, such as killings and a multitude of locusts that destroy both crops and animals. 

Wolves shall also cause harm to men. There shall be the digging of pits to lead forth streams <note>likely referring to the construction of irrigation ditches or wells to combat the drought mentioned earlier</note>, and there will be an increase of water along with coldness in the spring quarter. The air of the summer quarter shall be mild, and there will be much blowing of western winds. There shall be the building of water-conduits and a vehement cold in the winter quarter, but a temperance of the air in the autumn quarter. There will be an increase in plantings and seeds. 

The prevailing fashion of clothing among the people shall be garments that resemble dung in color <note>original: "fimo in colore"; likely referring to earthy, brownish, or ochre tones</note>; and there shall be a time of peace for the King of Babylon.

Let us say, therefore, when those significations we have mentioned occur, it signifies that in the cities over which the ruler <term>almuztauli</term> <note>original: "almuztauli"; a Latinization of the Arabic *al-mustawlī*, referring to the planet that holds the most "dominion" or power over a particular place or time</note> presides, there will be many births of kings and tyrants. It signifies their appearance with strength, audacity, vigor, and fearfulness: as well as much austerity and magnanimity, a love of fame, a love of making war, fraud, deception, distress, and sadness. There shall be the mockery of men and a desire for gold, silver, and precious stones. Illnesses shall happen to men, especially in the stomach and the mouth, along with the arrival of buboes <note>original: "bubonum"; glandular swellings or tumors, often a symptom of infectious disease</note> and a great many deaths. There will be vehement heat in the summer quarter, and the west wind shall blow at its end incessantly. There shall be many rains and strong cold in the winter quarter, with few winds at its end. There shall be few fruits from the trees, yet planted crops shall be improved, and the waters of the springs shall diminish. There shall be a dark garment over it <note>this likely refers to the symbolic "clothing" or atmospheric color associated with the sign's influence</note> consisting of clothing of diverse colors, such as white, ash-gray, and red.

If it is in the northern parts, it signifies a change of the air and its heat, and if it is in the southern parts, it signifies humidity of the air. And because, with God’s help, we have now explained what we wished to set forth, let us therefore complete this fifth distinction.

### ¶ The Seventh Distinction regarding the significations of Libra ♎, following the same manner as the previous.

Let us say, therefore, that when the significations we have mentioned are present, it signifies that there will appear in the cities over which the <term>almuztauli</term> <note>original: "almuztauli"; an Arabic astrological term for the "predominator" or the planet that holds the most power or influence over a specific place or chart</note> rules: the laws of the prophets and their decrees, and faith, and discourse among the people. There will be the building of churches and houses of prayer, along with their servants and guardians, who shall possess a goodness of countenance and a beauty that will be found within them. It also signifies generosity, justice, equity, and truth; as well as speech, explanation, the receiving and giving of gifts, and the buying and selling of goods. Furthermore, it indicates progress in arithmetic and geometry, and the exposition of various sciences: of songs, melodies, and other things besides these. 

There shall be a sense of solace, joy, dancing, and delight; people will gladden one another, and money will multiply in their hands. They will build cities, great halls, gardens, and pleasant places; and there will be settlements with the cultivation of the local surroundings. There will be a transformation of things with speed, moving from one state of being to another, and a general participation in these changes. While there may be the occurrence of misfortunes and celestial <term>impressions</term> <note>the influence or "imprint" that celestial bodies are believed to exert on the earthly realm</note>, there will be safety for women in childbirth and for their children. 

The air will be darkened hour after hour, and there will be an increase in the blowing of hot, poisonous winds in the spring quarter, as well as hot, poisonous winds in the summer quarter. There will be balance in the autumn quarter and a moderate temperament in the winter quarter. It will also happen that the citizens will more frequently use black-colored clothing. Joy shall come to the King of Babylon <note>In medieval astrology, "Babylon" often referred to Cairo or the general region of the Near East</note> when the greater luminary <note>The Sun</note> is directly in the sign of Cancer (♋); he will rejoice and see that which gladdens him. Movements and hunting will increase, yet death will fall upon his common people.

And when the degrees of the <term>ascendant</term> <note>the sign or degree rising on the eastern horizon at a specific moment</note> are in its first third, or there is a <term>direction</term> <note>a method of calculating future events by "moving" planets forward</note> in it, or a <term>profection</term> <note>the shifting of a point in the chart by one sign per year to time events</note> reaches it, or any <term>almuztez</term> <note>original: "almuztez" or "almubtez"; the planet with the most essential dignity or strength at a specific point</note> reaches it, it signifies a good <term>complexion</term> <note>the balanced "makeup" or temperament of the atmosphere</note> of the air. It is likewise in its second and third sections. If it is in its northern parts, it signifies the blowing of winds; and if it is in its southern parts, it signifies a multitude of clouds. And since, with God’s help, we have now set forth what we wished to explain, let us therefore conclude the seventh distinction.

# ¶ The Eighth Distinction regarding the significations of Scorpio, following the same manner as the previous.

It also signifies prisons and prisoners, distress and sorrows, as well as betrayal, accusation, corruption <note>original: "mixturatio"; literally a mixing, often referring to the corruption of substances or humors</note>, infection, and illnesses.

### Ninth Distinction: On the figures of Sagittarius and what is like it.

Let us say, therefore, that when the significations of kings which we have narrated occur in this sign, there shall appear in the cities over which the <term>almustauli</term> <note>original: "almustauli"; an Arabic-derived term referring to the 'predominator' or the planet with the most power and influence over a particular place or chart</note> rules: the strength of kings and nobles, and their foresight will appear superior to the foresight of the common people. There shall be much military force and iron in the instruments of war, the governance of soldiers, and both deceit and ingenuity. There will be generosity, as well as the gathering and dispersal of wealth. One will find cleanliness in food, drink, clothing, and in all things. Consequently, illnesses and a "fervor of the blood" <note>likely referring to high fevers or inflammatory conditions</note> shall follow the people, and the pain of pregnant women shall be intensified. Wolves and wild beasts will multiply. 

The spring quarter will be characterized by many clouds, rains, and winds; the autumn quarter shall have temperate winds; and the winter quarter will be cold and humid. Good things and bread will multiply, as will the worms of the earth, and perhaps this signifies the destruction of the ears of grain. A dark or tawny color <note>original: "color fuscus"</note> will come upon those citizens. The King of Babylon shall suffer the sickness of fever and a pain in the head, and it shall last for 22 days. Enemies will surround the lands of the Romans, which will be a source of grief to them. War will follow in the land of <term>Aldeilen</term> <note>original: "aldeilen"; referring to Daylam, a mountainous region in Northern Iran known for its fierce warriors</note>, and perhaps they will suffer from pain in the joints <note>likely arthritis or gout</note>, but it shall be removed from them. 

And when the degrees of the ascendant are in its first third <note>The first ten degrees, or "decan," of the sign</note>, or if its direction or any <term>almubtez</term> <note>original: "almbutez"; the Almuten, or the planet with the most essential dignity</note> is found there, or if the <term>profection</term> reaches it, it signifies humidity in the air. If it is in the middle third, it signifies a good temperament of the air. If it is in the final third, it signifies heat. If these occur in its northern parts, it signifies the blowing of winds; if in its southern parts, it signifies humidity in the air and a great speed of change. 

And as we have reached that which we wished to explain, let us therefore complete the Ninth Distinction.

### Distinction II. On the significations of Aquarius in a similar manner.

Let us say therefore that when the significations are as we have predicted, it signifies that there will appear in the cities over which the <term>almustenli</term> <note>original: "almustenli"; an Arabic-derived term (al-mustawlī) referring to the planet that acts as the "ruler" or "predominator" over a specific location or house.</note> prevails, the labor of building cities and strong halls, the digging of rivers, the planting of trees, and thoughts regarding the dead and the state of the fathers who have passed. There will also be the working of glass and similar items made from soft substances, and misfortunes shall come upon travelers. The spring quarter shall be moderately cold, with intense heat in the summer quarter, and the autumn quarter shall lean toward heat. In this time, lightning, thunder, and rain shall multiply; and the cold shall be strengthened in the winter quarter with much snow and the blowing of eastern winds. These damp conditions will harm the vineyards, yet it shall be a fertile year. Grain, dates, and the planting of trees shall increase, though harmful locusts will also multiply among them. Every land situated upon the seashores or riverbanks will suffer terrible damages, such as droughts, illnesses, and the like. Goodness and joy will multiply in the land of the Arabs, and the Romans <note>In this medieval context, "Romans" typically refers to the Byzantine Empire or the Christian territories of the West.</note> will contend with their enemies.

If the degrees of the Ascendant are in its first third <note>Medieval astrologers divided each 30-degree zodiac sign into three 10-degree "thirds" or decans.</note>, or if there is a "direction" within it, or any <term>almubtez</term> <note>original: "almubtez"; the planet with the most combined dignity or "victory" over a specific point.</note>, or if the profection <note>A predictive technique where a point in the chart is moved forward by one sign per year.</note> reaches it, it signifies moisture in the air. And if it is in the second third, it signifies a mixing of the air. And if it is in the final third, it signifies the blowing of winds without intermission. If it is in the northern parts, it signifies the blowing of winds; and if it is in the southern parts, it signifies clouds. And because, with God’s help, we have now explained what we intended to set forth, let us therefore complete Distinction II by His power.

### The divisions of the principal kingdoms of the earth and what they receive from the signs.

The divisions of the earth are four, of which the first is **Antioch** and the part of the East: and it has from the signs Cancer ♋, Leo ♌, and Virgo ♍, and from the planets the Sun ☉ and Mercury ☿. ¶ The second is **Alexandria** and that which is around it from the southern part: and it has from the signs Libra ♎, Scorpio ♏, and Sagittarius ♐, and from the planets Venus ♀, the Moon ☽, and Saturn ♄. ¶ The third is the part of **Armenia** and those which are in the West: and it has from the signs Capricorn ♑, Aquarius ♒, and Pisces ♓; and from the planets Venus ♀, Jupiter ♃, Mars ♂, and the Moon ☽. ¶ The fourth is **Constantinople** from the North: and it has from the signs Aries ♈, Taurus ♉, and Gemini ♊; and from the planets Mercury ☿ and Venus ♀. ¶ And the Indians estimated that the beginning [of the world] was on a Sunday with the Sun rising; and there is between them—that is, between that day and the day of the Flood <note>original: "diluuij"</note>—seven hundred and twenty billion, six hundred and thirty-four million, eighty-two thousand, seven hundred and fifteen days; which will be one billion, nine hundred million, three hundred and forty thousand, nine hundred and thirty-eight Persian years <note>original: "anni persici"</note> and three hundred and forty-four days. And the Flood occurred on a Friday, on the twenty-seventh day of the month of Rabi' I <note>original: "rabe primi"; the third month of the Islamic calendar</note>, and it is day 29.

### ¶ The third distinction concerning the nature of the knowledge of the significations of Mars (♂) according to that method.

Since we have previously set forth in the second distinction how we may know the specific properties of the significations of Jupiter (♃), let us therefore treat in this distinction how we may know the specific properties of the significations of **Mars** (♂) according to that same method.

Let us say, therefore, that when those significations which we have recounted belong to it <note>Mars</note> and are applied to the human species, it signifies many wars and conflicts rising up against kings, and the anger of princes. Furthermore, there will happen to certain men from these things a sudden, swift, and heavy death; and illnesses which will be accompanied by **tertian fevers** <term>tertian fevers: fevers that peak every third day, historically associated with malaria</term>, especially for those advanced in years. Some people will also incur punishment, insults, and violence, as well as being cast out from the protection of the law <note>original: "exitum a lege," referring to outlawry or exile</note>, along with a multitude of blocked roads <note>original: "abscisarum viarum," suggesting routes made impassable by bandits or war</note>; and there will be the shedding of blood and the occurrence of fires <note>original: "combustionis"</note> along with **plague-sores** <term>bubonibus: buboes, or the glandular swellings characteristic of the plague</term> in many **climates** <term>climates: a traditional geographical system dividing the world into seven latitudinal zones</term>.

¶ But the proper significance of the **Sun** (☉) specifically regarding the *ibuzeihe* <note>original: "ibuzeihe"; a Latinized Arabic term referring to the Sun’s entry into the first minute of Aries, which marks the start of the astrological year</note> in one of the **revolutions** <term>revolutions: "reuolutionū"; the completion of a planetary cycle, specifically the Solar Return used to predict the events of the coming year</term> is that it portends the king shall suffer harm, and death shall come to the common people. It signifies a mixing of enemies from all horizons; the year will be unfruitful, wild beasts will multiply, and certain kings will go to visit others. Blood shall be poured out in the western parts, and killings will multiply there; the noble shall become poor, and the poor shall become rich.

Truly, its significance according to the manner of its **mixing** <note>original: "commixtionis"; the blending of a planet's influence with others through astrological aspects</note> when it enters the beginnings of the revolutions we have previously mentioned, is that the planets indeed associate themselves with it—or without it—when their distance to those places follows in all revolutions. A diversity of meanings does not arise except from the timing of the **ascensions** <term>ascension: "ascēstionū"; the rising of zodiac signs or planets above the eastern horizon at a specific time and location</term> and the variety of planetary positions and the cities of their **ascendants** <term>ascendant: "ascendentiū"; the sign or degree of the zodiac rising in the east at the moment of the revolution</term>, as we have stated before. For this reason, we have recalled its significance over the **accidents of the lower world** <note>original: "accidētia inferioꝝ"; earthly events and physical changes in the "sublunary" realm, as opposed to the unchanging celestial heavens</note> because it is equidistant to those very parts we have already mentioned. However, the significance of its equidistance in all signs is of greater importance than that alone.

### Distinction 4: On the quality of the knowledge of the property of the signification of **Venus** (♀) according to that same principle.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration of the Roman goddess Venus. She is depicted seated in a triumphal chariot on the right, wearing a winged helmet and holding a spear. **A**fter, therefore, we have set forth in the third distinction the significations of **Mars** (♂) and that which is designated by a singular designation <note>original: "designatione singulari"; referring to the Sun's unique role as the primary indicator in an annual chart</note> by the property of the **Sun** (☉). Let the significations of **Venus** (♀) therefore be remembered in this distinction according to that same principle. Let us say, then, that when those significations which we have narrated are hers, and they are appropriated to her according to the **human species** <term>human species: "speciem humanam"; an astrological category where planetary effects are interpreted specifically through human social roles and health</term>, it signifies the appearance of moderation and providence, and good intention in matters of faith, and the death of certain wise men, especially from among the citizens of **Babylon** <note>Babylonia was often cited in medieval texts as a primary seat of astrological knowledge and a key geographical referent for omens</note>; it also signifies the revelation of sublimation and the elevation of kings, and that men shall bring much honor to one another, and the appearance of joy and the prosperity of marriage, and a multitude of children. Yet, perhaps men will divorce their wives, and young women will suffer miscarriages <note>original: "aborſum"; can refer to both natural miscarriage and induced abortion</note> from fornications, and envy and harm to bodies will be multiplied. 

And if her signification be according to the **species of beasts** which men use, it signifies their multiplication and their profitability. And if her signification be according to the **earthly element**, it signifies the well-being of seeds, trees, and fruits. And if her signification be according to the **aquatic element**, it signifies an abundance of waters and the safe passage of ships upon the seas.

### Book V.

### Distinction six on the quality of the knowledge of the significance of the Moon according to the same source

**A**fter we have thus set forth in the fifth distinction the knowledge of the quality of Mercury’s significance, let us therefore treat in this distinction the significations of the Moon. Let us say, then, that when its significations are as we have said and they are assigned according to the human species <note>original: "secundum speciem humanam"; in astrology, certain signs of the zodiac are classified as "human" (like Aquarius or Gemini). Predictions are interpreted differently depending on whether the planet is in a human, animal, or elemental sign.</note>, it signifies slaughter between kings and the common people, and much evil in everything, and the appearance of robbers, and harm in all cities, and many distresses which will come to kings because their women will be opposed to them and will help them little on account of their great number; and their fraud will be revealed to them, along with the fact that the Romans will be rebellious, and the Arabs will wage war against the Persians, and there will be great harm from wolves. If its significance should be according to the animal species <note>original: "secundum speciem bestialem"; signs representing animals, such as Aries (the ram) or Leo (the lion)</note>, and especially those animals which men use <term>beasts of burden|livestock and animals used for labor or transport</term>, it signifies an occurrence of death among them. If its significance should be according to the aerial element, it signifies many rains. If its significance should be according to the aquatic element, it signifies much water and floods.

### Book V

After we have previously set forth in the sixth distinction how we might know the properties of the significations of the Moon individually, when it was equidistant <note>original: "equidistans"; referring to a specific astrological alignment or aspect</note> to all signs according to the nature of the mixture: let us therefore treat in this distinction the significations of the two nodes <term>nodes: the two points where the Moon's orbit intersects the ecliptic; the north node was often called the Dragon's Head and the south node the Dragon's Tail</term> and of stars having hair <term>comets: from the Latin "stellarum comas," literally "hairy stars," a common historical term for comets</term> when they are equidistant from all signs before they are deprived of their specific properties in their significations, like all the planets we have discussed before.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration of a ram, representing the zodiac sign Aries, walking towards the right.</image-desc>

¶ We say, therefore, that when the north node is equidistant to the sign of **Aries** <note>represented by the symbol Y in the original</note>, it signifies the elevation of nobles and great success beyond that which had come from the death of certain noble kings, as well as the changing of affairs and the arrival of a king. ¶ And if the south node should be equidistant to it, it signifies that kings and princes shall harm the common people, and that many of the common people shall be opposed to him, along with the fact that certain subjects and low-born men shall be raised up from their stations; these men will disdain to obey their prelates <note>high-ranking church or civil officials</note>, and perhaps poverty, fraud in business, and the death of oxen, sheep, and camels shall follow.

¶ And if any of the stars having hair <note>comets</note> should appear in equidistance to it, it signifies detriments occurring to the King of Babylon <note>often used here to refer to the regions of Mesopotamia or Cairo</note> and wars with the falling away into hatred, and battle between the King of the Persians and other kings. Battles shall come between the Greeks and the barbarians, and the citizens of Italy shall fight with the citizens of Alexandria; the Romans shall unsheathe their weapons, and terrors shall come to the citizens of Persia and the citizens of Syria, with much shedding of blood because of them. The affairs of the Romans shall follow misfortune and turmoil in their kingdom, along with detriment that will come to the citizens of the Turks <note>original: "thurcorum"</note>, great drought, pains of the eyes, the death of oxen there, the destruction of the great men, and the elevation of the wicked and the low-born. There shall be many mines of gold and silver, and a superfluity of heat in the summer quarter. ¶ If it should appear in the eastern region and the Sun is equidistant to the sign of Aries, it signifies that hatred shall fall between the citizens of Persia and many regions shall obey the King of Babylon. And if it should appear in the western region, it signifies that the greater part of the noblemen shall follow after kings whom they will abhor due to misfortunes; slaughters shall come to the citizens of the western part, along with much rain, floods of rivers, and the falling of snow.

### Book 6.

In the ascendants of the revolutions <note>the "revolution of the year" refers to the solar return chart used to predict the year's events</note>; or in the signs of division <note>original: "signis diuisionis," likely referring to the "bounds" or specific segments of the zodiac</note> and especially in the **term** <term>term: a specific set of degrees within a zodiac sign governed by a particular planet</term> itself, or if it were with the lords of some of these, it signifies that many anxieties and wars shall come to them. This will occur because of those rising up against them; and their envy shall multiply, as will injury among men; and perhaps it signifies their slaughter. ¶ If the person was born from among the middle class or from the lowest order, it signifies many enemies for them, and that they will encounter horrible misfortunes due to these causes. And because, with God’s help, we have now explained what we intended to set forth, let us complete the seventh distinction of the fifth treatise, which is its conclusion.

¶ In the name of the Lord, the merciful and pious: The sixth treatise on the nature of the knowledge of the properties of **inferior accidents** <note>original: "accidentium inferioꝛū," referring to earthly events or the changing fortunes of individuals as opposed to the "superior" eternal stars</note> which come from the impression of certain individual bodies in the revolutions of the years, regarding the **mamareth** <term>mamareth: a transliteration of the Arabic "mamar," meaning the transit or passage of a planet over a specific point, such as the degree of a previous conjunction</term> of the stars rising over others; and it contains twelve distinctions.

<meta>This page continues the transition into the sixth treatise, moving from the general introduction of "mamareth" (transits) to the specific mathematical and astronomical methods for calculating the movement of planets in their orbits. It establishes the rules for determining whether a planet is ascending toward its furthest distance (apogee) or descending toward its nearest (perigee), which in turn influences the strength of its astrological "impression" on earthly events.</meta>

the **transits** <term>transits: translated from the Latinized Arabic "mamareth," referring to one planet passing over or occulting another</term> of some stars over others at the time of the revolutions of the years; for this was one of the concluding parts of what we wished to demonstrate concerning the nature of the knowledge of the meanings of conjunctions in this book, with the help of God.

Let us say, therefore, that there is no individual body among the celestial spheres that is not higher than that which follows it in order. They do not utilize transits over one another except in the sense that when some of them are joined to others—and are equal in longitude and latitude, and in their descent and equality—this will cause the covering of the lower by the higher. This will be among the occurrences signaling the beginnings of changes in **earthly events** <note>original: "accidentia inferiora," literally "lower accidents," referring to the changing circumstances of the material world</note>.

¶ Now, the knowledge of how this is known in the superior stars <note>Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn</note> and the two luminaries <note>the Sun and the Moon</note> is for you to consider their mean motion and their true position.

¶ If its true position is less than its mean motion, it is ascending from the middle of its zone toward the **furthest distance** <note>original: "longitudinem longiorem," or the apogee, where the planet is most distant from the Earth</note> of its orbit.

¶ If its true position is greater than its mean motion, it is descending from the middle of its zone toward the **lower distance** <note>original: "longitudinem inferiorem," or the perigee, where the planet is closest to the Earth</note> of its orbit.

¶ If the true position and the mean motion are equal in quantity, it will be in the middle of its zone. Then, after you have determined this, subtract the lesser of them from the other and multiply the remainder by 9; then divide it by 22, and what results from the division will be the amount of its ascension or descension in degrees.

However, when Mercury <note>symbol: ☿</note> or Venus <note>symbol: ♀</note> are oriental <note>rising in the east before the Sun</note> and their true position is less than the true position of the Sun <note>symbol: ☉</note> at that time, then they ascend from the middle of the zone toward the furthest distance of both their orbits. And if its true position is greater than the Sun's true position and it is occidental <note>setting in the west after the Sun</note>, it is descending from the middle of the zone toward the lower distance of its orbit. And if it is in direct alignment with the Sun and joined to it, it will be in the middle of its zone; afterward, take the difference between them and proceed with the same division and multiplication as performed for the superior stars.

The strongest significance of the superior bodies during the transits of some over others appears during a conjunction of equal distance <note>likely referring to an occultation or an exact alignment in both longitude and latitude</note>. In oppositions, however, and in **quadratures** <note>an aspect where two planets are 90 degrees apart</note> and other configurations, the significance of these will be of lesser appearance and weaker impression.

### Discourse on the **transits** <term>transits: from the Arabic "mamareth," referring to when one planet passes over the position of another in the sky</term> of **Saturn** <note>original symbol: ♄</note> over the planets.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration positioned to the right of the first paragraph. It depicts an enthroned male figure, representing the planet Saturn as a deity or personified influence. He is seated on a high-backed chair with a large six-pointed star above him to the right and the astrological symbol for Saturn (♄) below the star. The base of the chair is integrated with a wheel. Let us know, therefore, that if **Saturn** <note>original: ♄</note> should pass over **Jupiter** <note>original: ♃</note>, it signifies that the King of **Babylon** <note>often used in medieval texts to refer to the Sultan of Egypt or the region of Mesopotamia</note> will fight against many men because of the evil deeds that will appear to him in many of his cities. It also suggests a malice of custom along with great dryness, a scarcity of rain, and a great supply of grain in the harvests. ¶ And if he should pass over **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note>, it signifies many illnesses coming to children, along with many poisonous things in a time favorable to him, with a disturbance of the air and much dust. ¶ And if he should pass over the **Sun** <note>original: ☉</note>, it signifies the renewal of a king with wars among men, and death with a moderate amount of rain; and that the citizens of **Al-Ahwaz** <note>original: "alhauuez," a region in modern-day Iran</note> will fight with the Romans, and wars will come, with excessive death, a surplus of rain, and the blowing of winds of moderate movement. ¶ And if he should pass over **Venus** <note>original: ♀</note>, it signifies the renewal of a king with wars among men, and death with a moderate amount of rain. ¶ And if he should pass over **Mercury** <note>original: ☿</note>, it signifies the renewal of a king, and that the citizens of **Al-Ahwaz** will fight with the Romans, and many wars will come, with excessive death, a surplus of rain, and the blowing of winds of moderate movement. ¶ And if he should pass over the **Moon** <note>original: ☽</note>, it signifies many wars and a surplus of rain and the benefits they bring.

### Discourse on the **transits** of the planets over **Saturn** <note>original: ♄</note>.

When **Jupiter** <note>original: ♃</note> shall pass over **Saturn** <note>original: ♄</note>, it signifies the exaltation of the king over the common people, and a scarcity of his enemies, along with many terrifying rumors and lies; it also indicates the prosperity of the air and the blowing of **tempered** <note>original: "tpatonum," likely a contraction for "temperatorum"</note> winds during the harvests, and that his state shall be prosperous. ¶ And if **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> should pass over him, it signifies the sorrow of the King of **Babylon**, and perhaps a new king will be renewed; it also signifies excessive death among the citizens of the mountains, with a great blowing of poisonous winds, much rain, and a good summer. ¶ And if the **Sun** <note>original: ☉</note> should pass over him, it signifies that the Romans will enter **Armenia**, and **buboes** <note>original: "bubones," referring here to the swellings associated with the plague</note> will fall upon the citizens of **Al-Ahwaz**, with much rain and many harvests; it indicates prosperity in both places, though perhaps the grasses will be diminished. ¶ And if **Venus** <note>original: ♀</note> should pass over him, it signifies that the Romans will enter **Armenia**, and plague-sores will fall upon the citizens of **Al-Ahwaz**, with an unceasing blowing of northern winds and much water. ¶ And if **Mercury** <note>original: ☿</note> should pass over him, it signifies that same thing. ¶ And if the **Moon** <note>original: ☽</note> should pass over him, it signifies that the Romans go into **Armenia**, and the occurrence of death in **Al-Ahwaz**, and little rain.

# Discourse on the **transits** <term>transits: from the Arabic "mamareth," referring to the movement of one planet over the position of another</term> of **Mars** over the planets.

<note>This section describes what happens when the planet Mars moves across the positions of the other planets in the sky.</note>

And when **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note> is passing over the **Sun** <note>original: ☉</note>, it signifies an extreme occurrence of wars in **Babylon** <note>In this period, Babylon often referred to Cairo or the wider Mamluk Sultanate in Egypt</note> and injustices, and falsehood, and the selling of men to one another, along with a scarcity of heat and a good mixing of the summer quarter; it also signifies many flashes of lightning and a violence of winds uprooting trees and plants.

¶ And when it is passing over **Venus** <note>original: ♀</note>, it signifies many wars against the citizens of the mountains on the part of their enemies, and death to fall upon **owls** <term>bubones: great horned owls, often regarded as ill omens</term> and **birds of prey** <term>alhauuez: likely a transliteration of an Arabic term for a type of hawk or predatory bird</term>, and fires to come into the remaining regions, along with many horrible things and plagues; it also suggests prosperity for pregnant women, though with their own plagues arriving alongside a dryness of the air.

¶ And when it is passing over **Mercury** <note>original: ☿</note>, it signifies wars arriving in the land of **Jerusalem** and many enemies in the land of the **Arabs**, with a scarcity of rains and clouds, vehement heat, and little water in the springs.

¶ And when it is passing over the **Moon** <note>original: ☽</note>, it signifies the death of the **King of Babylon** and a separation among the citizens of Babylon, and many battles and wars in many lands and the taking of captives among one another, and excessive death in **Persia** and among the **Romans** <note>likely referring to the Holy Roman Empire or the Byzantines, depending on the source text's age</note> with the death of the king; and another king shall be renewed, and there shall be much rapacity of wolves, a sickness of four-legged animals, and a scarcity of moisture.

### Discourse on the **transits** of the planets over **Mars**.

**¶** And when the **Sun** <note>original: ☉</note> is passing over **Mars** <note>original: ♂</note>, it signifies humidity of the air. And when **Venus** <note>original: ♀</note> is passing over him, it signifies that death will come to certain queens <note>original: "regum mulieribus"; literally 'women of the kings'</note>, and it will be a heavy time for men and there will be destruction among women; it also signifies that citizens shall fight with the people of the mountains, and many armies will be moved, and there will be a battle between the Black peoples <note>original: "ex parte nigroꝝ"; likely referring to peoples of sub-Saharan Africa</note> and the peoples of the mountains, and they will destroy many regions with a multitude of waters and an excess of rain. **¶** When **Mercury** <note>original: ☿</note> is passing over him, it signifies a great and intense fear that occurs in many regions, along with fighting, destruction, discord, obstacles, and death in the land of the Romans, and especially among men, with the blowing of winds and much snow. **¶** When the **Moon** <note>original: ☽</note> is passing over him, it signifies much humidity and coldness.

## ¶ Discourse on the transits of the planets over **Saturn**.

¶ When **Venus** is passing over him, it signifies that the citizens of **Al-Ahwaz** will be prosperous, and many soldiers will be among them, with an abundance of rains.

¶ When **Mercury** is passing over him, it signifies the prosperity of the king of **Babylon**, and the unceasing blowing of winds.

¶ When the **Moon** is passing over him, it signifies a multitude of rains.

## Discourse on the transits <term>transits: from the Latin "mamareth," an astrological term derived from the Arabic "mamarr," meaning the passage of one planet over the position of another</term> of **Saturn** <note>original symbol: ♄</note> over the planets.

¶ We say therefore that when **Saturn** <note>original symbol: ♄</note> shall be passing over **Jupiter** <note>original symbol: ♃</note>, it signifies the moderation of the King of Babylon <note>Babylon was often used in medieval astrology to represent major Eastern powers</note>, and that he shall hold his kingdom by himself and place little trust in others. It also signifies many thieves and perverse people, a scarcity of rain, a lack of water, and many water-beasts such as frogs and similar creatures <note>original: "his silia," likely a transcription of "his similia"</note>. ¶ When he shall be passing over **Mars** <note>original symbol: ♂</note>, it signifies the commotion of the Turks and their deceit; that enmity shall fall among men; many locusts; and an excess and force <note>original: "firionem," likely meaning the intensity or flow</note> of rains. ¶ When he shall be passing over the **Sun** <note>original symbol: ☉</note>, it signifies the death of the wives of kings, and the occurrence of death in many regions <term>climates: from the Latin "climatibus," referring to the seven latitudinal zones of the known world</term> along with dryness of the air. ¶ When he shall be passing over **Venus** <note>original symbol: ♀</note>, it signifies a pestilence coming to the land of the Romans, and death with great heat and a lack of moisture. ¶ When he shall be passing over **Mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note>, it signifies a cause of death in many regions; for this reason, severe fevers will strike people, along with a scarcity of rain and moderate heat. ¶ When he shall be passing over the **Moon** <note>original symbol: ☽</note>, it signifies the death of certain wives of kings, and the occurrence of death in many regions with severe fevers, and with a scarcity of rain and water.

## Discourse on the transits of the planets over **Saturn** <note>original symbol: ♄</note>.

¶ And when **Jupiter** <note>original symbol: ♃</note> shall be passing over **Saturn**, it signifies that much slaughter shall occur among kings, and the death of the King of Babylon; that the mountain-dwellers shall make an assault upon the citizens of Babylon; the destruction of several regions; many births with a scarcity of rain and moisture; an increase in harvests; and that beauty shall be prosperous. ¶ When **Mars** <note>original symbol: ♂</note> shall be passing over him, it signifies many enemies rising up, a fall of locusts, moderate rain, and a scarcity of water. ¶ When the **Sun** <note>original symbol: ☉</note> shall be passing over him, it signifies a decrease of water and moderate rain. ¶ When **Venus** <note>original symbol: ♀</note> shall be passing over him, it signifies a prosperity of incessant rains, and that locusts shall greatly destroy the crops. ¶ When **Mercury** <note>original symbol: ☿</note> shall be passing over him, it signifies the health of the Roman king and the durability of his life, a scarcity of rain, and the movement of winds. ¶ When the **Moon** <note>original symbol: ☽</note> shall be passing over him, it signifies <note>original: "sigt," an abbreviation for "significat"</note> the miscarriage of pregnant women, a scarcity of harvests, an excess of rain, and much moisture.

### Discourse on the transit of the planets over the **Sun**.

### ¶ Discourse on the transit <term>transit: from the Latin "mamareth," an astrological term derived from the Arabic "mamarr," meaning the passage of one planet over the position of another</term> of **Saturn** (♄) over the planets.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration depicts a bearded man, representing the planet Saturn, seated on an ornate throne. He wears a hooded robe and holds an object, possibly a scythe or staff. ¶ I say that when **Saturn** is passing over **Jupiter**, it signifies the destruction of the land of Armenia and its endurance <note>original: "durabilitatem," likely meaning the duration of the hardship</note> for three years, with a scarcity of rains, drought, and an overflow of the waters of the seas. ¶ When he is passing over **Mars**, it signifies the destruction of many parts of the lands with vehement cold and its long duration—especially in the two seasons appropriate to him <note>likely winter and autumn, the seasons associated with Saturn's cold and dry nature</note>—and the widespread death of many trees. ¶ When he is passing over the **Sun**, it signifies the dryness of the air. ¶ When he is passing over **Venus**, it signifies that the soldiers of Armenia shall be moved to action, as well as a prosperity of rains and moisture. ¶ When he is passing over **Mercury**, it signifies that the citizens of Alhauez <note>original: "alhauez," likely referring to the region of Al-Ahwaz in modern-day Iran</note> will greatly attack their enemies; it also signifies that death will come to certain royal women, and there will be a wandering of travelers who, in their journeys, will corrupt the lands and their borders, accompanied by an excess of rain, many floods, and the violence of cold. ¶ When he is passing over the **Moon**, it signifies much moisture and many rains.

### ¶ Discourse on the transit of the planets over **Saturn**.

¶ And when **Jupiter** is passing over **Saturn**, it signifies that many regions shall raise an army against the land of the Romans and depopulate many of their villages <term>villages: from the Latin "aldeos," likely derived from the Arabic "al-day'a" via Spanish "aldea"</term>, with the destruction of Armenia and many infirmities. It signifies death among men with little moisture and few gusts of wind, though there shall be prosperity for the crops; and perhaps drought will come to the land of Alhauez. ¶ When **Mars** is passing over him, it signifies many gatherings, vehement heat, and cold in the two seasons appropriate to them, as well as the corruption of locusts affecting many harvests. ¶ When the **Sun** is passing over him, it signifies that there will be rains of a moderate nature. ¶ When **Venus** is passing over him, it signifies many misfortunes <note>original: "diversitates," here implying adversities or changes in fortune</note> for the soldiers of Armenia, with the occurrence of death and sickness among men; it also signifies that there will be rains and moisture, and their restoration. ¶ When **Mercury** is passing over him, it signifies that the citizens of Armenia will raise an army against their enemies with great pride in those regions; they shall destroy a portion of the lands for those reasons, amidst vehement cold and the flooding of rivers. ¶ When the **Moon** is passing over him, it signifies that the citizens of Armenia will attack their enemies and destroy the greater part of them, along with an excess of rain and much moisture.

### ¶ Discourse on the transit <term>transit: from the Latin *mamareth*, a technical term for the passage of one planet over the degree or position of another</term> of the planets over **Mars** (♂).

¶ And when the **Sun** (☉) is passing over **Mars** (♂), it signifies that many injustices will occur in Babylonia, along with lying and wars where men find no truth in one another. This is accompanied by humidity in the air and vehement heat in its proper season.

¶ When **Venus** (♀) is passing over him, it signifies the death of certain kings and many wars in the region, along with an excess of humidity.

## ¶ Discourse on the transit <term>transit: (original: "mamareth," a Latinized version of the Arabic "mamarr") refers to the movement of a planet through the same degree of the zodiac occupied by another planet or a significant point</term> of Saturn over the planets.

¶ And when **Saturn** is passing over **Jupiter**, it signifies the occurrence of misfortunes and hardships in many regions <note>original: "climatibus," referring to the traditional geographic zones or latitudes of the world</note>, many wars in **Babylon**, the death of its king, the spread of terrifying rumors, and destruction within that land.

¶ And when it is passing over **Mars**, it signifies that wars will break out between kings and there will be excessive death in some regions, along with violent winds in their seasons.

¶ And when it is passing over the **Sun**, it signifies the occurrence of death among travelers, accompanied by an excess of rain—though perhaps it will be moderate—and a scarcity of crops.

¶ And when it is passing over **Venus**, it signifies the death of certain royal women in shame <note>original: "verecundia," implying a disgraceful or scandalous death</note>, with a scarcity of rain but a good yield of crops.

¶ And when it is passing over **Mercury**, it signifies the occurrence of death among travelers and wars in many regions, with the unceasing blowing of winds and a small profit from the harvests.

¶ And when it is passing over the **Moon**, it signifies that death will fall upon livestock, along with an abundance of moisture and its persistence, and poor preservation of the harvests.

## ¶ Discourse on the transit of the planets over Saturn.

¶ And when **Jupiter** is passing over **Saturn**, it signifies that misfortunes, distress, and wars will come to the **King of Babylon**, along with severe drought for his citizens, many enemies, and hatred arising among men; yet there will also be a multitude of rains and their moderation.

¶ And when **Mars** is passing over him <note>referring to Saturn</note>, it signifies many illnesses in many regions and the unceasing blowing of winds with much dust, and a low price for grain <note>original: "vilitate annone," meaning a low market price for the year's food supply, usually indicating abundance but sometimes a lack of value</note>.

¶ And when the **Sun** is passing over him, it signifies that wars will break out between kings and the death of the **King of Babylon**, along with an excess of rain.

¶ And when **Venus** is passing over him, it signifies the occurrence of death among women—or that they will be killed by poison—along with a scarcity of rain and a goodness of the harvests.

¶ And when the **Moon** is passing over him, it signifies that kings will fight among themselves, accompanied by an excess of rain.

¶ Therefore, when it happens that the sign of profection <term>profection: a symbolic timing technique where a specific point in a birth or event chart is moved forward by one zodiac sign for every year of time passed</term>, or the ascendant of the revolution <note>the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment the sun returns to its starting position for the year</note> is the first house of the preceding beginnings <note>referring to the original chart of a city, reign, or event</note>: or it is the sign of the conjunction <note>likely the Great Conjunction of Saturn and Jupiter, which medieval astrologers believed governed long-term historical cycles</note>: or there were directions <term>direction: a method of timing life events by "moving" a planet through the zodiac at a rate of one degree per year</term> in that revolution according to what we have told, it signifies that which will appear in the regions whose significations belong to that sign. These include the goodness of livelihood and of the beginnings of works; and things are renewed, completed, and increased; and there is the use of dialectic, rhetoric, and the knowledge of sciences; and a great frequency of eating and drinking and gatherings; and buying and selling; and that their greatest desire is for colors mixed with black <note>Original: "coloribus pmixto nigro." Then you shall consider its lord <term>lord: the planet that "rules" the specific zodiac sign where the profection or ascendant falls</term> and judge according to the quality of its place in itself and in its orb. If Saturn (♄) be in it, there is much good in that year. If Jupiter (♃) be the conjunction sitting in it, it signifies the oppression of the common people, and the generation of plagues and sicknesses, and the destruction of many regions, and a scarcity of rain, especially in the first year.

### Fourth Section: Concerning the significance of the fourth house in the same manner.

After we have set forth in the third section the account of the significations of the third house according to what we have told, let us now treat in this section the account of the significations of the fourth house <note>The Fourth House, or *Imum Coeli*, represents one's roots, the father, immovable property, and the ultimate conclusion of matters</note> accordingly. ¶ We say, therefore, that when it happens that the sign of profection <note>A technique where the houses of a birth or event chart are advanced by one sign for every year of life</note> or the ascendant <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> of the revolution <note>The Solar Return chart, cast for the moment the Sun returns to its original position each year</note> is the fourth house of any of the preceding beginnings, or conjunctions, or a direction <note>A method of timing events by "moving" planets at a set rate</note>, or any celestial body sitting in it or in the fourth house of the revolution, it signifies that which will appear in the regions whose significations belong to that sign: the desires and building of churches, the seizing of lands and inheritances, and the discovery of hidden movable wealth <note>The Fourth House is traditionally associated with buried treasure and minerals</note>. It also signifies little movement, great foresight in those things which follow, and matters concerning death and its causes. Fathers and elders will be honored; and their greatest desire regarding colors will be for red. ¶ Then you shall consider its lord <note>The planet that rules the zodiac sign located on the cusp of the house</note> and you shall judge by it according to the status of its position and its condition within the celestial orb. ¶ And if it is sitting in the ascendant, it signifies distress that will come upon men at the end of the year. And if a conjunction <note>An alignment of two or more planets</note> is sitting in it, it signifies many changes and journeys, and the destruction of regions and cities in many climates during the fourth year.

### Seventh Section on the significance of the seventh house in like manner.

After we have previously set forth in the sixth section the significations of the sixth house according to what we have told, let us treat in this section the significations of the seventh house according to the same method. ¶ Let us say, therefore, that when it happens that the sign of profection <note>A technique where houses are advanced by one sign per year to time events</note> or the ascendant of the revolution <note>The astrological chart calculated for the year's "birthday" or return</note> is the seventh [house] of any preceding beginnings or conjunctions; or if there be a "direction" <note>An advanced timing technique in astrology</note> or any specific planet <note>original: "indiuiduorum", referring to individual celestial bodies</note> sitting in it or in the seventh of the revolution, it signifies that which will appear in the regions for which that sign has significance: much management <note>original: "dispensatio"</note> and desire for women, and weddings, and banquets, and privation because of those things; and travel, and change, and pilgrimage; and the fall of certain men and the rise of others; and much alteration and the denial of things, and much blaming of men, and the killing of men by one another, and a multitude of archery <note>original: "sagationū", likely a variant of sagittationum</note>; and desire in hunting and in buying and selling, and much thought concerning death and one's own affairs. And if it be of bad state, it signifies that they shall attack them, and hold them in hatred, and seize their kingdom.

### ¶ Ninth Distinction: On the significance of the ninth house, following the same pattern.

### [The Form of the Shift]

He declares it in this form, if it pleases God. The profection <term>profection: a method where a point in the birth chart is moved forward by one zodiac sign for every year or period of time</term> from the ascendant of the nation <note>original: *gentis*</note> from the incomplete year of Yazdegerd <note>Yazdegerd III, the last Sassanid King of Persia, whose era began in 632 CE</note> 141. This is the collective figure for the shift <note>original: *permutationis*</note> of the conjunction from the Water Triplicity <note>the signs of Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces</note> to the Fire Triplicity <note>Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius</note>. And this year reached from the ascendant of the conjunction of the race <note>likely referring to the Islamic or Persian peoples in this context</note> all the way to Cancer; and from the place of the conjunction up to Leo; and from the division <note>the *fardar* or specific time-lord period</note> up to the 19th degree of Scorpio. And the greater luminary <note>the Sun</note> was directly upon the first point of the vernal equinox <note>the start of Spring</note> in that year according to the 7th hour and a half of the 23rd day of *Bahzamech* <note>the Persian month of Bahman</note>; and the ascendant, the locations of the planets, the rule <note>original: *canon*</note>, and the orders are according to this form, just as it is written in the middle of it, if it pleases God.

¶ And because, with God’s help, we have already described the positions of the spheres at the times of the three beginnings from their universal impressions, and their directions <note>astrological "directions" used for timing events</note> are calculated up to the place of the profections in the *mamar* <term>mamar: an Arabic term for the 'passing' of years or a span of time</term> of the years. Therefore, what remains most necessary is to speak of the number of Persian years that occur between the year in which the Sun was on the first day of the years of Yazdegerd, so that the quality of the knowledge of profections may be made easier, wherein time affects that knowledge and the knowledge of the nature of profections and conjunctions follows.

¶ Let us say, then, that the time elapsed between the first day of the year in which the greater luminary <note>the Sun</note> was at the first point of the vernal equinox in the year of the "shift of the *almanar*" <note>referring to a major astrological cycle for a nation</note> and the first day of the Hijra <note>original: *algira*; the start of the Islamic calendar in 622 CE</note> is 51 years, 2 days, and 16 Persian hours. And from the first day of the Hijra <note>original: *alhigite*</note> to the first day of King Yazdegerd, son of Shahriyar <note>original: *filij sarach*; likely a corruption of Shahriyar</note>, there are 9 years, 11 months, and 9 Persian days. The total of this will be 61 years, two months, 12 days, and 16 hours.

¶ Therefore, when you wish to know the sign of the profection from the ascendant of the shift of the *almanar* from the Air Triplicity <note>Gemini, Libra, Aquarius</note> to the Water Triplicity—which signifies the nation in the *mamar* of the years—always add the years of Yazdegerd which exist between them and the first day of the nation's year. Begin to cast <note>to count forward</note> from Libra, and wherever it reaches, that is the profection from the ascendant of the nation. 

However, when you wish to find the profection from the sign of the nation's conjunction, the casting shall be from Scorpio. And if you wish for the profection from the sign of the revolution <note>the solar ingress into Aries</note>, the casting shall be from the sign of Gemini. And if you wish for the profection from the degree of direction, the casting shall be from the 20th degree of Pisces, allowing one year for every degree; and wherever it reaches, that is the degree of the division. 

And when it stands in the degree of profection at the hour in which the greater luminary is in the degree of the vernal equinox, then it is most necessary that they add 10 seconds to every degree which the Sun cuts through the degrees of the sphere, and all these shall be collected when it passes through the remaining signs at 5 minutes. This calculation should be used from the hour it passes through every division of the orbital divisions until it reaches the end of its divisions, which is the end of Pisces. 

The necessary addition to the degrees of profection is, as we have said, 5 minutes for every whole degree of the sign. In this way, one may know the ascendants of the *firdaria* <term>firdaria: a system of planetary periods or "time lords" assigned to specific years of life or history</term> extracted with the twelve-fold division from the sign of the profection, and its angles from the ascendant of the *almanar*, and the agreement of the degree of profection and its angles, and which degree of profection and its angles [relate] to the sign of the *almanar*, demonstrating the health from the ascendants of the years and hours in which individuals of the earth are affected.

And when certain higher planets agree in the times of revolutions with the testimonies of the significations of the **firdaria** and other systems, that prediction is stronger in its configuration and more certain to come true, by the will of God and His help.

->**The work of Albumazar on the great conjunctions ends happily: through the diligent correction of Master Johannes Angelus, a most skilled man; and by the exceptional industry and marvelous printing art of Erhard Ratdolt, a clever man, in which he—formerly of Venice, now most famously excelling at Augsburg <note>original: *auguste vindelicoꝝ*</note>—completed this on the day before the Kalends of April [March 31], 1489.**<-
